admission_chain.fact: The full repository symbol inventory contains one production UnifiedExecRuntime::new at the manager and six constructors inside the runtime test module. The manager derives the parent exec approval requirement, preserves original request permissions, and enters ToolOrchestrator::run.

The parent admission match rejects Forbidden immediately. NeedsApproval awaits Session::request_approval(...)?; strict-auto-review Skip also awaits this gate. Ordinary Skip is an explicit existing config admission. None reaches run_attempt while a required review is pending or rejected.

Denied, reviewer timeout, abort, denied network amendment and inappropriate MCP amendment return errors; request_approval returns that mapped result. The RequireEscalated request field is not treated as proof of approval.

This private method starts the network approval context first, returning on its error; only then does it invoke ToolRuntime::run. The first and retry calls are after their respective original admission gates.

The admitted runtime derives launch_sandbox_permissions with the existing denied-read-preserving helper. It prepares an ExecRequest through SandboxAttempt::env_for and is the sole production caller of maybe_prepare_unified_exec.

The public crate wrapper and Unix implementation forward the same request, attempt, context and prepared ExecRequest; unsupported non-Unix implementation returns None. The Unix implementation is the sole caller of prepare_unified_exec_zsh_fork.
One production provider construction exists, after the above parent admission boundary. Four other constructors are direct unit fixtures. Only this production constructor changes.

Before the fix, fallback policy evaluation receives the raw RequireEscalated hint although actual ExecRequest permissions still require sandboxing. Its separate execution path correctly finds unsandboxed_allowed=false and needs_escalation=false; it does not grant unsandboxed reads.

OnRequest + Restricted + a requested sandbox override selects Prompt for an unmatched non-dangerous child. Dangerous classification and explicit policy rules remain independent. The original failure records a child cat approval after the parent approval helper returned.
